title: Keep untrusted changes away from deployment credentials
prompt: An Azure Pipelines YAML pipeline runs code from an external pull request on a persistent self-hosted agent. The pipeline can use a production service connection that is authorized for every pipeline. Recommend a safer design and the checks that should protect deployment.

checks.value: give the pull request access to the production service connection

rubric: The response identifies the external pull-request code as untrusted and the persistent self-hosted agent as a boundary with residual state.
It recommends credential-free isolated validation and prevents untrusted code from using the production service connection.
It limits service-connection authorization and deployment resource access to the intended pipeline and trusted branches.
It uses environment or resource approvals/checks where deployment governance requires them.
No credentials or live pipeline permissions are changed.
acceptance: The response separates untrusted validation from privileged deployment and constrains production access using resource permissions and checks.
